turns.prompt_text: what temperature do you need to be to be sick
turns.response_html:
A medical fever is generally defined as 100.4°F (38°C) or higher.

While 98.6°F is the traditional average, your "normal" can range between 97°F and 99°F depending on the time of day. If you feel unwell but your temperature is lower than 100.4°F, doctors often call this a "low-grade" fever.

Fever Thresholds

Measurement MethodFever Temperature
Oral (Mouth)100.4°F (38°C)
Rectal / Ear100.4°F (38°C)
Armpit99.4°F (37.4°C)

Note: For adults, a fever of 103°F (39.4°C) or higher warrants a call to a doctor. For infants under 3 months, any temperature of 100.4°F or higher is a medical emergency.
